assertions_contracts.best_practice: Consistent with the official precondition guidance fetched in this pass: require validates arguments, check validates state, and JVM assert is not production validation - exactly the guide's Sec.7 table.
assertions_contracts.evidence: Official exceptions page freshly fetched: its precondition table assigns require to argument/input validity and check to state validity, matching the guide; no contradiction in the 2.4 release material. Upgraded in confidence from run 1, where this page was not re-fetched.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: Assertions for internal facts, normal error paths for expected external failures, require for API-contract arguments, check for broken internal state, KDoc on public items stating contract and bounds, warnings as errors on the pinned toolchain.

bounded_work.best_practice: Tiger Style strictness: no official Kotlin source fetched in either pass prescribes application-level budgets, and none forbids them; the guide's bounds are a house policy layer over the language, not a language claim.
bounded_work.evidence: Fresh full read confirms the bounded-work text is unchanged from run 1; nothing in the freshly fetched 2.4 release, conventions, or coroutines material contradicts it. Verdict follows the cross-guide convention for uncontradicted house policy (stricter than default is not a contradiction).
bounded_work.guide_position: Bound loops/retries/queues/collection growth/coroutine fan-out with named unit-carrying limits; reject before expensive allocation; bound compressed/expanded sizes and retained output.

concurrency.best_practice: Matches the official coroutines model: structured concurrency, where new coroutines launch only in a CoroutineScope that defines their lifecycle, parents wait for children, and parent cancellation cancels children recursively.
concurrency.evidence: Official coroutines-basics page freshly fetched and states the structured-concurrency principle in those terms; guide Sec.10 is unchanged and aligns with it, including its cited runBlocking/Channel/withTimeout contracts.
concurrency.guide_position: Structured concurrency: every scope owned, no GlobalScope for app-owned work, cancellation cooperative/prompt and cannot publish partial effects, bounded channels, dispatcher choices documented, freshness tokens for stale results.

error_handling.best_practice: No official source contradicts the guide; the fetched exceptions page sanctions its core distinctions (require for arguments, check/error for state, precondition functions throwing IllegalArgumentException/IllegalStateException).
error_handling.evidence: Exceptions page freshly fetched for this pass (in run 1 it was not); its precondition-function table and try/catch/finally treatment match guide Sec.7, including the warning shape around runCatching capturing cancellation, which is a guide strictness addition, not a contradiction.
error_handling.guide_position: Sealed result types (not exceptions) for expected failures, require for API-contract arguments, check for broken internal state, assert not relied on for production validation, rethrow CancellationException, runCatching captures cancellation warning.

formatting.best_practice: The official Kotlin coding conventions prescribe four-space indentation with no tabs and the naming scheme the guide uses (UpperCamelCase types, lowerCamelCase functions/properties, uppercase underscore-separated names for true constants).
formatting.evidence: Conventions page freshly fetched for this pass (in run 1 it was not, hence unverified there): its Formatting section states the four-space/no-tabs rule and its Naming rules state the camel-case and constant conventions the guide Sec.5 restates. The guide's 100-column target is a house addition on top, not a conflict. The unnamed formatter tool is scored under static_analysis, not here.
formatting.guide_position: Four spaces, 100-column target, idiomatic naming (UpperCamelCase types, lowerCamelCase, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constants), one pinned formatter configuration (tool itself unnamed - see static_analysis).

memory_ownership.best_practice: The official Native memory-manager page confirms the guide's characterisation: objects live in a shared heap reachable from any thread and are collected by a tracing garbage collector; nothing in it suggests foreign resources are managed for the programmer.
memory_ownership.evidence: Memory-manager page freshly fetched for this pass (in run 1 it was not, hence unverified there): shared-heap plus tracing-GC description matches guide Sec.9 verbatim in substance.
memory_ownership.guide_position: JVM/Native GC manages objects not sockets/transactions/native buffers/GPU work; use 'use'/try-finally, explicit commit/flush, no finalizer reliance, copy at ownership boundaries, Native memory manager described as a shared heap with tracing GC, not a borrow checker.

security.best_practice: No official source contradicts this; the 2.4 stdlib security-support policy (an 18-month window per release line, with simultaneous fix releases across supported lines) strengthens the case for staying on the supported line the guide now pins.
security.evidence: Release-process page freshly fetched: standard-library security support starts with 2.4.0 with an 18-month window per line, and the 2.4 line is supported to December 3, 2027 - the rationale the remediated baseline table now cites.
security.guide_position: Null-safety is not authorization/deadlines/secrets; parameterized queries, TLS/identity libraries, no secrets in logs/bundles/argv/mobile bundles, outbound-destination restriction, dependency/Wrapper verification-metadata review, never disable TLS.
